h: Say It Right, Then See It All
p: First things first: it's pronounced Cul-lane, not Cul-zee-an, and the locals will thank you for getting it right. The castle was the seat of the Kennedy family, the Earls of Cassillis, and Robert Adam reworked an older tower house into the clifftop mansion you see today in the late eighteenth century. It's been in the care of the National Trust for Scotland since 1945.

Beyond the castle walls, the estate has some lovely corners that many day-trippers miss. Hunt out the Walled Garden, the Camellia House and the Fountain Court, then follow the paths to the Deer Park, where the kids can spot red deer. Down below the castle, there are caves in the cliffs that have their own smuggling tales attached. On a clear day the views out to Ailsa Craig and the Isle of Arran are superb, so make sure your camera has plenty of battery.
Plan for a full day if you can. It's easy to underestimate how far apart things are, so bring snacks, water and footwear you can walk a few miles in.

There's more to see around Maybole too. Crossraguel Abbey, the striking ruins of a medieval monastery, sits just outside the town and is a peaceful stop. And don't miss the Electric Brae on the coast road nearby, where an optical illusion makes the slope seem to run the wrong way. Stop at the marked spot and see if your car appears to roll uphill. Kids think it's magic.
